reviewer.note: Round 3 review at 8c212777 (PR #450), docs/reviews/2026-11-08-crossroads-placed.md, round 3. Answered: each tub has its own planting (geranium, daisy, lavender, marigold, ivy, herbs) in scalloped clumps with dark pockets (XR2-T5 fixed); the body now has a lit west, body and dark east, a hairline crack with a lit lip and a few pits. Still failing: the body is three or four straight vertical bands under a full-width ruled dark line, a box planter rather than a vessel, with one-tone runs of 118 texels (XR2-T1 asks none over 40); the lime bloom is still mostly a 2-row bar with drips under the rim (XR2-T2 partly); the lower-right corner is still a distinct near-black block (XR2-T3 partly); the soil shows as a dark 1-row slot under the rim, not a 2 px soil band under a lit inner wall (XR2-T4 partly). Cluster noise rose to 39.9 % (was 30.6 %; Eastward's props median 29 %, fault line 48 %): part of the bar's rise is grain, not structure. Bar 0.66 -> 0.86. Compared with the Eastward 13 bell and 17 churns at x1.37. Fix list: XR3-T1 to XR3-T4.
fix_list: XR3-T1: draw the body as a fired-clay vessel, not banded boards: let the lit west, body and dark east meet in a soft stepped curve (2-3 texel steps, not straight vertical edges), drop the full-width ruled dark line under the rim to a shadow that thins toward the lit west, and break every one-tone run over 40 texels with sibling-tone clay clusters (not value grain: keep cluster noise at or under 40 %)
XR3-T2: lime bloom as ragged pale clusters of 2-4 texels that wander under the rim and down one side, different on every tub; no 2-row bar with drips
XR3-T3: no distinct near-black block in the lower-right corner: let the belly's shade fade along the base row in 2 tones, and if a chip is wanted, give it a lit lip
XR3-T4: show the soil as a 2 px band with clods between the clumps and the far inner wall lit 1-2 px above it (not a 1-row dark slot)
